## Design

### 2026-10-05 – I tried to understand the basics of KiCAD and how to place the components in the schematic editor. I struggled a little to figure out the basics (such as placing wires and importing footprints). I lea

**1.42h**

I tried to understand the basics of KiCAD and how to place the components in the schematic editor. I struggled a little to figure out the basics (such as placing wires and importing footprints). I learned how to make a schematic diagram of the different components (pressing A in order to add a new component and P for power supply/grounding). Learning how to connect the wires without it going all over the place took some trial and error but I eventually figured out the best way was to finish a wire before doing the next connection. I also researched what the individual components were and what they did. Importing the footprint gave me a bit of trouble but I eventually figured it out through troubleshooting online.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/ce72520b-664d-4dcd-85bb-09707065056e/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-05 – ![1000155672](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/92251555f3957d78a70c01924e71d22dd3e241a4bb779d50a810ba5f92f82fa7.jpg)

**2h**

![1000155672](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/92251555f3957d78a70c01924e71d22dd3e241a4bb779d50a810ba5f92f82fa7.jpg)

Figured out how to get the star shape (after an INCREDIBLE amount of trial and error). Arranged the components onto the star shape and connected them. The star is easier to draw if I use a polygon instead of the line tool as i discovered after a bit of struggling. Connecting the wires was fairly straightforward. Following this,  I browsed the internet for the parts that might be necessary and created the rough parts list (subject to change). This served to be quite a challenge as getting the materials where I live might be slightly over the allocated budget (I will continue looking into it). I also got stuck with the programming because I was unsure how to proceed, therefore, I watched a few youtube tutorials and set up the app on my laptop. Now that I've understood the basic aspects tomorrow I'll start working on Sunbie!!

### 2026-10-11 – Firmware

**1h**

Firmware
This entry details my actions on the firmware, the modifications I have made and what I spend my coding hours on.  I had to swap out the Xiao ESP32-CS to waveshare ESP-32-C3-zero and also change on of the sensors the accelerometer from MPU6050 to an ADXL345 for cost reasons. This meant that I had to go through the code and make several modifications to it in order to make it workable.
I had the bright idea to add a health bar and then add another menu option. However, this genuinely was a hassle and a half to fix up because so many of the beginner code's menu options relied on there being 4 menu options. (the guide mentioned that but I thought it wouldn't be that bad ToT). Spoiler alert it very much was.

I also added new features and reactions because I felt like not much was being done with the DHT11 readings (they were just displayed on stats I believe). Therefore, I tried to add a too hot/too cold reaction.

![pet tempearture and sick](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/e59babf5c2fefb833e259a543f9c12fe234537f0d64e2b84224e9210eeb00c2c.png)

![Temperature reactions](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/5f0af19cbbaa44944ad76072561004a4c91825ffcb4750201c4e5f14f7e78be9.png)

I also added a pieze passive buzzer which enabled me to add sounds to my Sunbie (I added notes to played on opening menu and notes with each reaction), which once again I VASTLY underestimated how long that would take ++ how hard that would be but I got it done (I think?)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/b46e45551953fe77d874cdcc0e09ea9fc5f60e08fcc4889308ef3043cc7e379f.png)
Other than that I basically just went over the code, understood what it did and made modifications wherever necessary. I also added a musical notes special effect as I thought that would be fun.

![special effect](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/aecf0f6a602062fc834541afc64d1f229ba26fb9cc8aac568420a99d00443f64.png)

THIS TIME HAS BEEN UPDATED UNDER "SOFTWARE" ON HACKATIME.
hours 1-2: making modifications to the code wherever necessary and going over the whole code to ensure that I didn't miss anything ++ typing it out (I decided the most efficient way to make the changes I wanted was this ++ I wanted to practise making my own firmware instead of just copying the file)
hours 3-4: Adding the additional effects that I wanted to add ++ bitmap images
hours 5-6 : Adding sound effects and stuff
hour 6+ : Going over my code, debugging and logic checking

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/7740c0333ef1429006cfbb2307d2fbb14acc41e99d7fb833b1d2dde6a453c805.png)
